name: move_pose
description:
Submit a complete pose target through the Supervisor.
Use when: moving the public TCP to a stated position and orientation. Send one or both arms under targets; an omitted arm is not commanded. Each arm names its two choices as enums -- position_mode (hold_current, absolute, delta) and orientation_mode (hold_current, absolute_quaternion, axis_angle_delta, world_axes) -- and sends that mode's fields beside them in targets.<arm>. absolute takes position_m; delta takes translation_m and position_frame; absolute_quaternion takes orientation_xyzw; world_axes takes approach_world and jaw_line_world; axis_angle_delta takes rotation_axis, rotation_angle_deg and orientation_frame -- rotation_angle_deg is in DEGREES, and no field here takes radians. To hold one half while changing the other, set its mode to hold_current. Label the target free_space, precision or contact_approach by physical intent, not by controller name. speed (optional, beside targets; it applies to every arm the call moves) is fast, normal or careful. fast is the default and the normal choice. normal (about 0.3 m/s and 60 deg/s) is for moves near objects, and while holding an object (fast's hard accelerations can make it slip). careful (about 0.1 m/s and 20 deg/s) is for the last 1 to 3 cm of an approach, contact or placing; for that last bit, slow_approaching: true (fast or normal) slows only the final 2 cm of the same move to careful and is preferred over a whole careful move; use it when placing a held object. Slower speeds use more physics steps, so use them only where they help. These are guidance, not enforced. Instead of speed you may give speed_m_s, any number above 0: the top speed of the TCP in m/s, with a turn-rate cap of 200 deg/s per m/s (at least 20 deg/s), both reached in 0.25 s. Whatever the speed, each joint's own speed is the real ceiling (at most 108.9 deg/s on this arm, at every speed): where a hand move needs large joint turns, or for a high speed_m_s, the arm moves slower than asked, so a fast request may not be reached; a slow one practically always is. last_action_effect.detail.motion.speed.planned_peak_linear_m_s says the top speed a global route's plan reaches.
Effect: compiles the request once. free_space always uses global CuRobo; precision uses global CuRobo and may add one bounded 10 mm/5 degree local settle; contact_approach up to 10 mm/5 degrees is local, while a larger contact approach globally reaches a pre-contact pose and locally executes only the final 3 mm/2.1 degrees. A precision change that rotates by at most 15 degrees while moving at most 5 mm is local. Every stage uses measured convergence and a local failure never silently falls back to global. The speed holds on every route. A global route is timed so the TCP keeps the speed's caps, one joint target per 4 ms physics step (fast: no Cartesian speed limit, the joints alone); when both arms move they share one timeline, and the shorter move is slowed to it. A bounded local stage, which follows no planned path, instead spreads each servo step over as many physics steps as the same linear and turn speeds need, with no ramps. Before anything moves, a global route is refused (plan_rejected, with no controller write) when its TCP would turn more than 45 degrees beyond the turn from its start to its planned end orientation (paced_path_wrist_unwind: the wrist would unwind the long way round, and the other paths to the same pose tried first do too; ask for a target orientation nearer the current one) or when it needs more than 5000 physics steps at the requested speed (paced_motion_budget: use a faster speed or split the move); last_action_effect.detail.motion.refused gives the numbers. A move is never cut part way, so it never stops in the middle of a wrist turn.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival, and available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion, force/progress evidence and truthful unknown values. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. The later receipt's last_action_effect.detail.motion reports speed (speed -- custom with speed_m_s -- speed_m_s when given, slow_approaching, the caps linear_m_s, angular_deg_s and joint_speed_deg_s and, for a global route, planned_peak_linear_m_s and planned_peak_angular_deg_s: the top speed and turn rate the planned path reaches under every cap, joints included, the largest over the moved arms; with slow_approaching also slow_approach_m and the slow caps) and, for a global route, wrist (under each moved arm's name, the last wrist joint from the path's start through every planned physics step: start_deg, end_deg, min_deg, max_deg, travel_deg and min_limit_margin_deg to its joint limit, since the two ends alone can hide a swing; and that arm's TCP path_turn_deg and requested_turn_deg), planned_ticks and duration_s, the physics steps and seconds of the shared timeline. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: ask the policy to choose CuRobo versus local DLS; change an exact requested orientation; command a gripper; move an omitted arm; infer contact, retention or task success; retry a failed local stage through another backend.
On error: Refused: an empty targets map or an arm outside left and right; an unknown field, a mode without its companion fields or a field of another mode, each naming the field; hold_current for both halves of one arm, a target equal to the measured pose, a rotation_angle_deg outside [-180, 180] or an orientation_xyzw whose norm lies outside [0.98, 1.02], each as invalid_motion_arguments without a field; a target outside the bound action workspace (workspace_bounds) unless the TCP is already outside it and the target only reduces the violation; a placement waiting at its pre-release stop (skill_sequence_paused); the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). Also refused as invalid_motion_arguments naming the field: a speed other than fast, normal or careful; a speed_m_s that is not a number above 0 or comes with a speed; slow_approaching with speed careful or with speed_m_s at or below 0.1 (it has no effect there). Rejected before any controller write, as plan_rejected: two arms labelled with different interactions; any target outside the bound action workspace, with no exception; every admitted Top-K plan failing validation, which includes a planned TCP step above 80 mm, a planned path leaving the action workspace by more than 0.1 m, and the two arms' 45 mm link spheres coming within 5 mm of each other -- or, when they start closer, closing in by more than 1 mm -- with the other arm checked even when it does not move. position_mode delta without translation_m is refused at targets.<arm>.translation_m; a field belonging to another mode is refused by name. planner_failed means the planner found no path, and its failure code says why: goal_unreachable, goal_in_collision, goal_below_support, start_in_collision or path_blocked; plan_rejected means zero controller writes; not_reached means execution started but measured convergence or endpoint verification failed. Use the named phase and fresh evidence rather than repeating the same target blindly. Failure diagnosis: planner_error identifies a failed planner service or implementation, not an unreachable target; invalid_start_state requires correcting the measured start; planner_failed reports ordinary search failure. not_reached preserves endpoint and controller evidence independently of official task termination. Read the fresh observation before proposing another action. Numerical inputs follow compute's Use when rule; send every value in this tool's declared units and frame. Before submission each target gets a read-only reach pre-check, compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.reach_along_request. On this backend it is one IK solve by the planner a global route uses, from the measured joints, with joint limits, self-collision and the collision world global routes avoid, and no trajectory is planned (ik_model robotwin_reach_ik_depth_world_v1). That world is rebuilt for each request from the current depth images of every camera: the robot removed, the other arm standing at its measured joints, the space around the goal hand cleared (contact at the goal is not checked), a held object moving with the hand, and space no camera sees, such as behind objects, counted as free. A target with a fingertip more than 1 cm below the supporting surface under it is refused before planning. The bounded local segments do not check the world. matches_move_pose_admission is false: for free_space this is the solver move_pose's global route uses, but move_pose also plans a trajectory and validates it, so it can still refuse a target reported reachable; contact_approach and small precision turns run locally and do not solve this exact target. If the target does not solve, it also reports the farthest solving fraction of the straight path from the current pose, and that pose. It never blocks or changes the move. When the target does not solve, reach_along_request also carries nearest_reachable_orientation: the smallest turn of the requested orientation (15 to 75 degrees in 15-degree steps, about axes perpendicular to the approach axis) that the same pre-check solves with the grip-centre TCP held where the request put it, as a pose with approach_world and tilt_from_straight_down_deg, or none_within_sweep; endpoint IK only, with the pre-check's error. compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.observed_clearance (also on move_to, rotate_wrist and rotate_pitch): the jaw footprint's lowest point at the target (fingers, plus the held object's localized extent when the jaws hold a named target) minus the highest surface the current depth images show beneath it or within radius_m; negative means that surface is higher; occluded surfaces are unknown; not a collision check. The jaws count as holding when the last gripper command was close and the measured jaw separation exceeds 3 mm, which does not confirm a grasp. world_axes compiles approach_world (the grip-centre TCP's local +X) and jaw_line_world (its local +Y) into orientation_xyzw. compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.target_axes_world, on move_pose, move_to, rotate_wrist and rotate_pitch, gives the submitted orientation's world approach and jaw-line directions. Fixed texts stated once here and left out of results and effects: compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.observed_clearance.claim_boundary (move_pose, move_to, rotate_wrist and rotate_pitch) is "From the current depth images and their calibration only; points inside the measured jaws, the held object and the space above them are excluded as robot, other robot links are not; occluded surfaces and object undersides are unknown; points up to the footprint's top within radius_m count; not a collision check or a contact prediction, and the move is submitted unchanged."; compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.reach_along_request.claim_boundary is "Read-only IK at sampled points of the straight interpolation from the measured pose to the target; reachability is not proven monotone between samples, and no path, collision, payload or arrival claim. One IK solve per pose by the IK solver of the global planner move_pose uses, seeded from the measured joints or a chained query's solution, with joint limits, self-collision and a collision world built from the current depth images: the robot removed, the other arm at its measured joints, the space around the goal hand cleared, a held object moving with the hand, and space no camera sees counted as free. The solution's grip centre is checked against the arrival bound. It plans no trajectory and runs no plan validation, so move_pose can still refuse a pose reported reachable, and a finite seed search can miss a solution." for an unsolved target and, for a solved one, the same text from "One IK solve" on; reach_along_request.nearest_reachable_orientation.claim_boundary is "Read-only IK at each candidate endpoint by the same reach check as reach_along_request (its ik_model and matches_move_pose_admission apply), from the measured joints: the requested orientation turned about axes perpendicular to its approach axis, holding the jaw centre; no path, collision, payload or arrival claim, and an orientation outside the sweep may solve.".

targets.description: Sparse per-arm targets. An omitted arm receives no new target and is not commanded.

left.description: The left arm's target. Omit to leave the left arm uncommanded. Null means omitted.

position_mode.description: Choose with its companion fields in the same target: hold_current takes no position fields; absolute REQUIRES position_m; delta REQUIRES translation_m AND position_frame. A mode alone supplies no values.

position_m.description: REQUIRED with position_mode=absolute. [x,y,z] in world metres. Omit for other position modes. Null means omitted.

translation_m.description: REQUIRED with position_mode=delta, together with position_frame. [dx,dy,dz] in metres. Omit for other position modes. Null means omitted.

position_frame.description: REQUIRED with position_mode=delta, together with translation_m. world uses fixed world axes; end_effector uses current controlled-frame axes. Never inferred. Omit for other position modes. Null means omitted.

orientation_mode.description: Choose with its companion fields in the same target: hold_current takes no orientation fields; absolute_quaternion REQUIRES orientation_xyzw; axis_angle_delta REQUIRES rotation_axis AND rotation_angle_deg AND orientation_frame; world_axes REQUIRES approach_world AND jaw_line_world. A mode alone supplies no values.

orientation_xyzw.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion. Unit quaternion [x,y,z,w]. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

rotation_axis.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=axis_angle_delta, together with rotation_angle_deg, orientation_frame. An x, y or z axis in orientation_frame. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

rotation_angle_deg.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=axis_angle_delta, together with rotation_axis, orientation_frame. Signed DEGREES, not radians. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

orientation_frame.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=axis_angle_delta, together with rotation_axis, rotation_angle_deg. world or current end_effector axes. Never inferred. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

approach_world.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=world_axes, together with jaw_line_world. World direction [x,y,z] of the approach axis. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

jaw_line_world.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=world_axes, together with approach_world. World direction [x,y,z] of the jaw line, made perpendicular to approach_world. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

interaction.description: Physical intent, never a controller name. Omitted means free_space. Null means omitted.

right.description: The right arm's target. Omit to leave the right arm uncommanded. Null means omitted.

position_mode.description: Choose with its companion fields in the same target: hold_current takes no position fields; absolute REQUIRES position_m; delta REQUIRES translation_m AND position_frame. A mode alone supplies no values.

position_m.description: REQUIRED with position_mode=absolute. [x,y,z] in world metres. Omit for other position modes. Null means omitted.

translation_m.description: REQUIRED with position_mode=delta, together with position_frame. [dx,dy,dz] in metres. Omit for other position modes. Null means omitted.

position_frame.description: REQUIRED with position_mode=delta, together with translation_m. world uses fixed world axes; end_effector uses current controlled-frame axes. Never inferred. Omit for other position modes. Null means omitted.

orientation_mode.description: Choose with its companion fields in the same target: hold_current takes no orientation fields; absolute_quaternion REQUIRES orientation_xyzw; axis_angle_delta REQUIRES rotation_axis AND rotation_angle_deg AND orientation_frame; world_axes REQUIRES approach_world AND jaw_line_world. A mode alone supplies no values.

orientation_xyzw.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion. Unit quaternion [x,y,z,w]. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

rotation_axis.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=axis_angle_delta, together with rotation_angle_deg, orientation_frame. An x, y or z axis in orientation_frame. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

rotation_angle_deg.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=axis_angle_delta, together with rotation_axis, orientation_frame. Signed DEGREES, not radians. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

orientation_frame.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=axis_angle_delta, together with rotation_axis, rotation_angle_deg. world or current end_effector axes. Never inferred. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

approach_world.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=world_axes, together with jaw_line_world. World direction [x,y,z] of the approach axis. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

jaw_line_world.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=world_axes, together with approach_world. World direction [x,y,z] of the jaw line, made perpendicular to approach_world. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

interaction.description: Physical intent, never a controller name. Omitted means free_space. Null means omitted.

speed.description: Optional; default fast (the normal choice). normal: about 0.3 m/s, for moves near objects and while holding an object. careful: about 0.1 m/s, for the last 1 to 3 cm of an approach, contact or placing. Slower speeds use more physics steps. Leave it out when you give speed_m_s. Null means omitted.

speed_m_s.description: Optional, instead of speed: the top speed of the TCP in m/s, any number above 0 (turn rate capped at 200 deg/s per m/s, at least 20 deg/s). Each joint's own speed (at most 108.9 deg/s on this arm) stays the ceiling, so a high value may not be reached; last_action_effect.detail.motion.speed.planned_peak_linear_m_s says what a global route's plan reaches. Slower speeds use more physics steps. Null means omitted.

slow_approaching.description: Optional; default false. true slows only the last 2 cm of the path to the careful speed inside the same move (with speed fast or normal, or speed_m_s above 0.1; refused with careful). Preferred over a whole careful move for the end of an approach, contact or placing. Null means omitted.

reach_along_request.description: Read-only reach pre-check of the submitted target by this backend's reach check (ik_model), from the measured joints. matches_move_pose_admission says whether that check is the IK move_pose admits through for this request; when it is not, the check is a reference only. When the target does not solve, the straight interpolation from the measured pose is sampled.

nearest_reachable_orientation.description: The reachable turn of the requested orientation with the smallest angle, holding the nominal jaw centre, from read-only IK at the endpoint.

observed_clearance.description: Read-only, from the current depth images: the jaw footprint's lowest point at this target minus the highest observed surface beneath it or within radius_m; negative means that surface is higher. Not a collision check.

held_object.description: null unless the jaws measure as holding: the target the policy named when they closed and whether its localized extent is part of the footprint.
null unless the jaws measure as holding: the target the policy named when they closed and whether its localized extent is part of the footprint.

target_axes_world.description: World directions of the approach axis and jaw line of the submitted target orientation, computed from its compiled quaternion.
